nodes.label: MCP server for the collection (add_words) design doc
Option A: new Auth0 API per environment (chosen)
nodes.rationale: Auth0's Default Audience is tenant-wide by construction (audience belongs to the request, not the client), so Option B's blast radius cannot be engineered away; A pays one new API per environment for an MCP token that is useless anywhere else.

nodes.label: Option B: reuse existing Auth0 audience (superseded)
nodes.rationale: Mechanically broken as first conceived (compatibility profile on breaks resource->audience mapping without an existing API; profile off yields an opaque token jose cannot verify); the working variant needs a tenant-wide Default Audience, making an MCP token a fully valid /api/v2 token.

nodes.label: add_words_to_collection MCP tool
nodes.rationale: Batch-shaped because resolve_words already accepts an array; dedupe by clientDedupeKey before the RPC and group output by id, since two inputs can legitimately collapse onto one word id.

nodes.label: Dynamic Client Registration is an open endpoint (risk)
nodes.rationale: Turning DCR on lets anyone register a client against the tenant, a documented abuse vector whose Auth0 mitigations are Enterprise-only.

nodes.label: Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) as the scaling answer
nodes.rationale: Unlike DCR, CIMD has no open registration endpoint — the client publishes a metadata document and the tenant admin imports it, keeping the tenant admin-controlled while still giving clients like ChatGPT (which offers no client_id field) a usable identifier.

nodes.label: Finding: ElevenLabs tutor agent is not a viable first MCP consumer
nodes.rationale: ElevenLabs' MCP integration authenticates with a workspace-level static secret, not per-user OAuth, so it cannot act as a specific learner — later reversed by docs_2026_08_28_elevenlabs_mcp_in_code once static-token auth made a fixed identity the design.
